title: api: add schema versioning, beta headers, and backward-compatibility shims for OpenAI-compat layer
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Adds a first-class API schema versioning mechanism and beta header signaling to support a phased rollout of API surface changes (streaming stability fixes, tool/function-calling structured output improvements, and OpenAI compatibility layer updates) while preserving backward compatibility for existing clients. Motivation: recent changes to the structured output and function-calling shapes required a safe migration path for customers and SDKs; this PR introduces X-Redwood-API-Version and X-Redwood-Beta request headers, response deprecation warnings, and server-side backward-compatibility shims that translate between v1 (legacy OpenAI-compatible shapes) and v2 (new structured output with richer tool metadata). Design: 1) Request header X-Redwood-API-Version: clients can opt into explicit schema versions (e.g. "2026-02-15" or "2026-02-15-beta"). 2) X-Redwood-Beta: boolean-style header to enable beta behavior without changing client schema, used for trialing streaming stability and function-calling improvements. 3) Response header X-Redwood-Deprecation-Warn: informs clients when using deprecated shapes; contains a short code and ETA for removal. 4) Compatibility shims: runtime layer that rewrites incoming/outgoing payloads to preserve OpenAI-compatible message/chat/envelope formats when clients request v1 compatibility; also performs KV-cache-aware streaming boundaries adjustments to reduce partial-event fragmentation. 5) OpenAI-compat layer updates: added a conversion module that maps new structured tool outputs to the classic "function_call"/"message" formats and vice versa, plus deterministic ordering for multi-tool responses to keep SDKs stable. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout in Canary -> Dedicated -> Hosted; telemetry hooks added to track header adoption and failure modes. Testing: unit tests for header parsing, JSON-shim translations, streaming chunk boundaries; integration tests for SDKs (python/ts) exercising both v1 and v2 traffic shapes; added e2e test that replays recent production requests with both headers enabled. Docs: added versioning doc + migration guide and SDK helpers. Backwards compatibility: non-breaking by default (defaults to v1 behavior), warns callers via headers and logs, and provides a migration timeline. If enabled with explicit version or beta header, runtime immediately serves the new shapes. This PR focuses on the API contract and server-side conversion; follow-up PRs will update SDK convenience helpers and examples to expose version headers more ergonomically.
